method: The authors develop a parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol achieving doubly polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: They prove that the proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with time overhead polylogarithmic in the circuit size, improving over previous polynomial overheads.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible with efficient parallel decoding, advancing the practicality of quantum error correction.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling limit, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors extend the Keldysh formalism to include Lindblad dissipators, introducing diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism yields a systematic perturbation expansion for Green's functions and correlation functions in driven open quantum systems, enabling calculation of steady-state properties and fluctuations.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information where dissipation and driving are unavoidable.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to engineer selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity gates for dual-rail superconducting qubits.
motivation: Dual-rail superconducting qubits show promise for error correction but require fast reset and state preparation. Selective transitions are needed to avoid leakage and crosstalk.
method: The authors propose a dual-driving scheme that dresses the two-qubit system and uses frequency-selective pulses to target specific transitions while suppressing others, analyzed via Floquet theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that selective transitions can be achieved with high fidelity and speed, reducing gate errors and enabling efficient reset protocols.
conclusion: The dual-driving approach provides a practical path to improve gate performance in dual-rail qubit platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperatures in guided wave propagation.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from purely spatial to spatiotemporal dynamics in multimode fibers, exploring equilibrium properties and the role of negative temperatures.
method: The authors use a wave turbulence approach to derive a kinetic equation describing the evolution of the spatiotemporal spectrum, and identify a Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium distribution with a chemical potential and temperature that can be negative.
result: They show that spatiotemporal thermalization occurs with a conserved wave action and energy, leading to equilibrium states characterized by positive or negative temperatures depending on the initial conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for understanding nonlinear wave propagation in multimode fibers, with potential applications in optical communications and laser systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of multi-site projection operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding by focusing on the role of noncommutativity among measurements.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index based on the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index sharply distinguishes between volume-law and area-law entangled phases, and that the transition occurs when the index changes from zero to nonzero.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a rigorous analytical tool for understanding measurement-induced entanglement transitions, offering new insights into the role of measurement in quantum dynamics.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior; the authors aim to characterize subsystem decoherence in a state-independent manner.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the quantum channel describing the reduced dynamics of a subsystem, analyzing its behavior in chaotic systems.
result: The purity of the Choi matrix serves as a probe of dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence, revealing signatures of chaos.
conclusion: The Choi matrix purity is a useful state-independent measure for studying decoherence and irreversibility in quantum many-body chaos, connecting to information thermodynamics.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that one-axis twisting dynamics, which typically require all-to-all couplings, can be realized in short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains to generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and spin squeezing.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) is a powerful method for generating quantum resources but requires all-to-all interactions, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by using short-range interactions.
method: The authors propose and analyze a protocol using short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains with engineered interactions to emulate OAT dynamics. They use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated with short-range interactions, achieving comparable performance to all-to-all OAT for sufficiently large systems. The generated entanglement and squeezing scale favorably with system size.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a practical platform for generating quantum resources via OAT-like dynamics, making it feasible for current quantum simulators without all-to-all connectivity.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a shortcut-to-adiabaticity protocol to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, achieving high efficiency and fidelity while reducing storage time.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting its speed. Accelerating the process causes losses due to non-adiabatic transitions.
method: The authors design a counter-diabatic driving field based on the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant to suppress non-adiabatic transitions, enabling fast and efficient storage.
result: The accelerated protocol achieves near-unity efficiency and high fidelity even for short storage times, outperforming conventional adiabatic EIT memory.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-performance quantum memories based on Rydberg EIT, beneficial for quantum networks.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the Lieb-Robinson bound and the energy gap scaling near criticality.
result: The precision per unit time is bounded by a constant independent of system size, revealing a trade-off between precision and measurement time.
conclusion: Critical quantum metrology cannot achieve Heisenberg scaling in finite time; the fundamental limit is set by the Lieb-Robinson velocity and critical exponents.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical learning on randomized measurement data to verify approximate k-designs, providing a practical certification method for random quantum states.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods are inefficient or require full state tomography.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on randomized measurements and classical machine learning to certify approximate k-designs without full state reconstruction.
result: The method is shown to be efficient and robust, requiring only polynomial resources in system size and achieving high accuracy in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a scalable and practical tool for certifying random state ensembles, with applications in quantum benchmarking and many-body physics.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted preparation and measurement devices, with applications to quantum error correction and entanglement distribution.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, especially in variational algorithms, error correction, and quantum repeaters.
method: The protocol uses a trusted preparation and measurement device to characterize and purify noisy states and measurements via a series of iterative steps, leveraging symmetries and post-selection.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements, significantly reducing the impact of preparation and measurement noise, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to mitigate preparation and measurement errors, enhancing the performance of various quantum information tasks without requiring full quantum error correction.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution in NMR detection of nuclear spin clusters, which is important for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use NV centers in diamond to polarize nuclear spins, combined with stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to perform sensitive NMR.
result: They resolve sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique enables detailed study of spin clusters in diamond, advancing applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a new secret-communication protocol based on paraparticle statistics, highlighting their potential for quantum information tasks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially enabling more practical quantum memories and processors.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function. They develop theoretical tools to compute it for various states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation, the compression rate for lossless compression, and the number of measurements needed for tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and practical measure of non-Gaussianity with direct operational interpretations, advancing the resource theory of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to optimize the control fields, achieving higher fidelity.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that can be detected and corrected.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by enabling error detection and correction.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into erasures.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, allowing parallel addressing.
result: Demonstrates that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed simultaneously without sacrificing cavity enhancement.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing offers a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom quantum processors.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems are limited by measurement-induced errors and long readout times; improving readout fidelity is crucial for quantum computing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to maximize the nondemolition nature, reducing measurement time and errors.
result: The protocol achieves a qudit readout fidelity of 99.61% while mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly enhances the performance of nondemolition measurements, offering a practical improvement for multilevel quantum systems in quantum information processing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing; this work aims to characterize the phase transition in random codes.
method: The authors analyze spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes and study the decoding transition using statistical physics and random matrix theory.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and suggest that random codes can achieve optimal performance near the transition.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and key rates, with security proofs approaching composable security. The review also covers measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with potential for integration into future quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols and evaluates their theoretical security and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges; the review highlights both opportunities and limitations.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing equivalence between two key tasks and providing efficient protocols for functions in certain complexity classes.
motivation: Characterizing the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation (NLQC) is known to be hard; the authors aim to circumvent this by studying relative hardness via reductions, similar to complexity theory.
method: The authors define resource-efficient reductions between NLQC tasks and prove that the two best-studied tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under O(log n) overhead reductions.
result: They obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P, and extend several properties from f-route to f-measure.
conclusion: The reduction approach simplifies existing proofs and provides new insights into the resource requirements of NLQC, advancing the understanding of quantum information processing in distributed settings.

title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent master equations from data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and dissipative dynamics of open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, but existing machine learning approaches often lack thermodynamic consistency.
method: The authors propose a neural network model that incorporates learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and linear coupling to the environment.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level systems and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating accurate and interpretable recovery of system parameters.
conclusion: The approach provides a physically principled, interpretable machine learning framework for learning open quantum system dynamics, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and control.

title: On The Addressability Problem On Css Codes
authors: Jérôme Guyot And Samuel Jaques
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2145 (2026).

Recent discoveries in asymptotically good quantum codes have intensified research on their application in quantum computation and fault-tolerant operations. This study focuses on the addressability problem within CSS codes: we ask what circuits might implement logical gates on strict subsets of logical qubits. With some notion of fault-tolerance, we prove several impossibility results: for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address a logical [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], or [MATH] to any non-empty strict subset of logical qubits using a circuit made only from 1-local Clifford gates. Furthermore, we show that one cannot permute the logical qubits in a code purely by permuting the physical qubits, if the rate of the code is (asymptotically) greater than 1/3 and the distance is at least 3. We can show a similar no-go result for [MATH]s and [MATH]s between two such high-rate codes, albeit under a more restrictive assumption on the circuit, which we call "global" (though recent addressable CCZ gates use global circuits). This work pioneers the study of distance-preserving addressability in quantum codes, mainly by considering automorphisms of the code. This perspective offers new insights and potential directions for future research. We argue that studying this trade off between addressability and efficiency of the codes is essential to understand better how to do efficient quantum computation.

.
tldr: This paper proves impossibility results for addressing logical qubits in high-rate CSS codes using local Clifford circuits, and shows that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is limited by code rate.
motivation: Understanding how to implement logical gates on subsets of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially with asymptotically good codes.
method: The authors use automorphism theory of CSS codes and combinatorial arguments to derive no-go theorems for addressability under fault-tolerant constraints.
result: For non-zero rate CSS codes, 1-local Clifford circuits cannot address logical X, Z, H, or S gates to strict subsets; permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is impossible if rate > 1/3 and distance ≥ 3.
conclusion: There is a fundamental trade-off between addressability and code efficiency, which must be considered for practical quantum computation.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment, with applications in open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses a structured environment as an entropy sink, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to manipulate its environment.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate it with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: The framework provides an intuitive picture of how repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment, and qualitative agreement with previous experimental results is found.
conclusion: Active control can enable new functionalities in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a generalized noncontextual framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; a locally-classical but contextual theory exists, decoupling local classicality from classical explainability.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality, and there is no straightforward link between local classicality and noncontextuality.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum walk on simplicial complexes that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Quantum walks on graphs have shown advantages, but extending them to simplicial complexes could unlock new quantum algorithms for topological data analysis and homology computation.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that operates on oriented simplices, using coherent interference to encode the combinatorial Laplacian and project onto its kernel (harmonic cycles). They also build variants for persistent Betti numbers, QMA-hard problems, and the high-dimensional Dirichlet problem.
result: The construction achieves apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup without quantum oracles, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide significant quantum advantages for topological data analysis and related computational tasks.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit symmetry to achieve exponential sample complexity improvements.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-inefficient without symmetry information.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry, using a dual formulation to analyze circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
authors: Guilhem Doat And Augustin Vanrietvelde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: This paper clarifies the differences between weak and strong symmetry constraints in quantum reference frame frameworks, linking them to the accessibility of global charge.
motivation: Different communities have developed non-equivalent frameworks for quantum reference frames, and the paper aims to clarify the mathematical and physical distinctions between them.
method: The authors analyze the mathematical differences between weak and strong symmetry constraints and show they correspond to whether the global charge is accessible to observers. They also introduce an operational scenario involving relativized interference measurement and classical communication.
result: The weak approach induces ambiguity in momenta and prevents reversible QRF transformations; the strong approach allows internal observers to measure the global charge under certain physical postulates.
conclusion: The choice of symmetry constraint has fundamental physical implications, and the paper advocates for the strong approach based on operational considerations.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions, with efficiency improvements and error correction analysis.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical due to high resource requirements. This work aims to bridge theory and experiment.
method: The protocol uses one-way functions and quantum bit commitment to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for resource estimation and error correction.
result: The proposed QOT protocol is more efficient than prior works and includes a detailed analysis of experimental errors and their mitigation, making it feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical QOT protocol that advances the state of the art in quantum cryptography, with clear steps toward experimental realization.

title: A Semantics For Counterfactuals In Quantum Causal Models
authors: Markus Frembs And Eric G Cavalcanti Ardra Kooderi Suresh
abstract: We introduce a formalism for the evaluation of counterfactual queries in the framework of quantum causal models, generalising Pearl’s semantics for counterfactuals in classical causal models, thus completing the last rung in the quantum analogue of Pearl’s ‘ladder of causation’. To this end, we define a suitable extension of Pearl’s notion of a ‘structural causal model’, which we denote analogously by ‘quantum structural causal model (QSM)’, and a corresponding extension of Pearl’s three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction. We show that every classical (probabilistic) structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and prove that counterfactual queries that can be formulated within a classical structural causal model agree with their corresponding queries in the quantum extension—but the latter is more expressive. Counterfactuals in quantum causal models come in different forms: we distinguish between active and passive counterfactual queries, depending on whether or not an intervention is to be performed in the action step. This is in contrast to the classical case, where counterfactuals are always interpreted in the active sense. Another distinctive feature of our formalism is that it breaks the connection between causal and counterfactual dependence that exists in the classical case: quantum counterfactuals allow for counterfactual dependence without causal dependence. This distinction between classical and quantum causal models may shed light on how the latter can reproduce quantum correlations that violate Bell inequalities while being faithful to the relativistic causal structure.
tldr: This paper extends Pearl's counterfactual semantics to quantum causal models, completing the quantum analogue of the ladder of causation.
motivation: Counterfactual reasoning is crucial for causal inference, but a quantum generalization was missing. The authors aim to provide a formal framework for counterfactuals in quantum causal models.
method: They define quantum structural causal models (QSMs) and a three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction, generalizing Pearl's classical approach.
result: Every classical structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and counterfactual queries agree with classical ones while being more expressive. Quantum counterfactuals allow counterfactual dependence without causal dependence.
conclusion: The formalism sheds light on how quantum causal models can reproduce Bell correlations while respecting relativistic causal structure, and it completes the quantum ladder of causation.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; this work fills that gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: Uses the tensor-product structure of a qubit as part of a larger composite system to derive the existence of a density matrix and Born's rule from probability assignments.
result: Successfully derives density matrices and Born's rule for a qubit, extending Gleason's theorem to the qubit case.
conclusion: The composite system axiom is sufficient to recover the quantum formalism for qubits, providing a foundational result in quantum information theory.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for nonequilibrium currents is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be insufficient when hidden conservation laws exist.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying how hidden conservation laws suppress directed transport.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents despite symmetry breaking, revising the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of nonequilibrium transport and highlights the role of conservation laws in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel and analyzes Gaussian quantum steering for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Gaussian quantum steering is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication, but realistic free-space channels introduce loss and noise that degrade steering. Understanding these effects is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors model the free-space channel including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence, and analyze the Gaussian steering of two-mode squeezed states after propagation through such a channel.
result: They quantify how steering degrades with increasing loss and noise, and identify regimes where steering can be preserved for satellite distances.
conclusion: The results provide guidelines for designing satellite-based quantum communication protocols that rely on continuous-variable steering.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles by controlling disorder statistics.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is fundamental for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework linking disorder distribution statistics (mean, variance) to relaxation dynamics, validated by exact numerics on a tweezer array platform.
result: They show that programmable disorder can control the crossover from fast to glassy relaxation, with implications for quantum memory and thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to engineer glassy dynamics in quantum simulators, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information storage.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit implementing the higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute geometric entanglement, using amplitude estimation and Grover-like search.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup over classical methods for certain cases, and is demonstrated on small examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical quantum algorithm for entanglement estimation, relevant to quantum information theory and quantum computing.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost, using stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can stay near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics with a Langevin equation and optimize a cost function that penalizes both distance from target and swimming effort.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a trade-off between localization accuracy and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in active systems, linking control and dissipation.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend equilibrium thermodynamic fluctuation theory to far-from-equilibrium settings after quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of transferred charge in integrable models, treating the quench as a source of ballistic transport and applying large-deviation theory.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations follow a universal scaling form governed by the GHD equations, with explicit results for the Lieb-Liniger model.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for non-equilibrium fluctuations, bridging quantum quench dynamics and statistical mechanics, and provides testable predictions for experiments.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to enable such control.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, using optical fields for quantum nondemolition measurements and manipulation.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum information processing with these systems.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical tool for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, advancing hybrid quantum systems that combine different atomic species.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson

result: They demonstrate suppression of measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The nonlinear coupling approach is effective for improving transmon readout, with potential applications in quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.

tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform, but achieving optimal sensitivity requires engineering non-classical states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by coupling the ion's internal spin to its motional state via a spin-dependent force, then apply a displacement and read out the spin state.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity at the standard quantum limit and beyond, demonstrating optimal estimation using spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with applications in force detection and quantum information.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and lack scalability.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The framework successfully identifies the number and parameters of spins in a simulated environment and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars

[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED systems with long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity-coupled Rydberg array model using mean-field and exact diagonalization techniques.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from kinetic constraints.
conclusion: Cavity-mediated interactions can engineer novel quantum phases and non-thermalizing dynamics in Rydberg arrays.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
